option.counterfactual: Bounded positive partial sums of projections in a finite AW*-factor do not necessarily force their normalized dimensions to tend to zero.
option.approach: Examine whether hypothetical counterexamples to projection exhaustion can be transported into a quasitracial ultraproduct. The purpose would be to obtain uniform projection dimensions and simplify the obstruction.

options.counterfactual: In every finite AW*-factor, projections with uniformly bounded positive partial sums must have quasitraces tending to zero.
options.approach: Try to prove this projection-exhaustion statement directly from continuous dimension and projection completeness. Then apply spectral cutoffs to the positive increments to exclude every positive value of eta.

options.counterfactual: In every finite AW*-factor, projections with uniformly bounded positive partial sums must have quasitraces tending to zero.
options.approach: Seek a finite quantitative packing bound for projections whose quasitraces are bounded below and whose sum is bounded above. Such a bound would establish exhaustion without assuming additivity of the quasitrace.

options.counterfactual: A quasitracial ultraproduct need not have all the AW*-factor and saturation properties used to construct a sequence without a least upper bound.
options.approach: Audit the ultraproduct construction separately for the annihilator property, factoriality, faithfulness, and the matrix extension of the quasitrace. Identify the first unsupported step before using the construction again.

options.counterfactual: There is a stronger universal obstruction than the two-increment bound, and every admissible eta must be at most one third.
options.approach: Analyze three or more positive increments using the matrix extension of the quasitrace. Look for a block-matrix comparison that yields a one-third bound without treating the quasitrace as additive.
